meta.titre: First Aid in the Home: Defining First Aid, Treating Common Injuries and Stocking a Kit
meta.sous_theme: Definition and aims of first aid, common home accidents, the pulse and the first aid kit

source.epreuve_titre: GCE O/L Food and Nutrition past paper (Cameroon)

sections.contenu_markdown: A child grabs a hot pot in the kitchen, a cousin cuts a finger on a tin, or an elderly relative faints in the heat. In such moments the first few minutes matter, and the person who stays calm and acts correctly can prevent a minor injury from becoming serious. Because accidents are so common in the home, the GCE asks you to define first aid, treat simple injuries, take a pulse and list the contents of a first aid kit. Paper 2 often asks for a fixed number of items or steps.

items: Blood carries oxygen and food around the body, and the heart pumps it through the arteries.
A burn damages the skin, and an open wound can let germs in.
Germs spread from dirty hands and dirty objects.

sections.titre: First aid: definition, treatment of common injuries and the kit
sections.contenu_markdown:
### Definition and aims
**First aid** is the immediate help given to a person who is injured or suddenly ill, using simple means, before a doctor or nurse arrives. Its aims are to **save life**, to **prevent the condition from getting worse** and to **help recovery**. A good first aider stays calm, acts quickly, sees to the most serious problem first, and sends for medical help when needed.

### Treating common home injuries
| Problem | First aid |
|---|---|
| Cut or bleeding | Wash your hands. Press firmly on the wound with a clean pad; raise the injured part; when the bleeding stops, cover with a clean dressing. Do not remove a pad that is soaked; add another on top. |
| Burn or scald | Cool the burn under cool running water for at least ten minutes; remove tight rings before swelling; do not burst blisters or put butter, oil or paste on it; cover loosely with a clean non-fluffy dressing. Serious burns need a doctor. |
| Fainting | Lay the person down, raise the legs, loosen tight clothing, give fresh air. |
| Nosebleed | Sit up, lean forward and pinch the soft part of the nose. |
| Sprain | Rest the part, apply a cold pack wrapped in cloth, bandage it gently and raise it. |
| Electric shock | Switch off the power before touching the person. |

### Taking the pulse
The pulse is the beat felt in an artery each time the heart beats. A home nurse takes it at the **wrist**, on the thumb side, using the fingertips (not the thumb, which has its own pulse). Count the beats for one full minute, or for 15 or 30 seconds and multiply. A healthy adult at rest has about 60 to 80 beats a minute. Exercise, fever and fear make it faster.

### Contents of a first aid kit
Adhesive plasters, sterile gauze dressings, cotton wool, bandages (roller and triangular), adhesive tape, antiseptic, scissors, safety pins, tweezers, disposable gloves and a thermometer. Keep the box labelled, dry and out of reach of small children, and replace used items.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked to define first aid or to outline a fixed number of kit items or steps.
variantes.contenu_markdown: A definition needs the key ideas: immediate help, to an injured or suddenly ill person, before medical help arrives. For "outline seven items" write seven different items, one per line, with a word on the use of each if there is room, for example "scissors, for cutting dressings and bandages".

variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked for mistakes to avoid or when judging a first aider's actions.
variantes.contenu_markdown: Do not move a person who may have a broken bone or neck injury unless there is danger. Do not give food or drink to an unconscious person. Do not put butter, oil or toothpaste on a burn. Do not give medicines you are unsure of. Do not leave the injured person alone. Call for medical help when the injury is serious.

sections.enonce_markdown: A girl pours boiling water on her forearm while cooking. (a) State four things that the person helping her should do. (b) State two things that should not be done. (6 marks)

etapes.action: Read the command words and the marks.
etapes.justification: "State" asks for short points; four points in (a) and two in (b) make six short answers for 6 marks, one mark each.
Boiling water causes a scald, which is treated like a burn.
First aid follows a sequence: stop the heat, cool, protect, get help.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Remove the girl from danger, cool the area, remove rings, cover, seek help.

etapes.action: Write the answer in complete points.
etapes.justification: Each point is a clear instruction.
etapes.resultat_markdown: (a) 1. Cool the scald under cool running water for at least ten minutes. 2. Remove rings, watches or tight clothing near the area before it swells. 3. Cover it loosely with a clean, non-fluffy dressing. 4. Take her to a health centre or send for medical help if it is large or deep. (b) Do not burst blisters. Do not apply butter, oil or toothpaste.

sections.conclusion_markdown: (a) Cool the scald with cool running water for at least ten minutes, remove rings and tight items, cover loosely with a clean dressing and get medical help if it is serious. (b) Do not burst blisters and do not apply butter, oil or toothpaste.

items.erreur_markdown: Pouring cold water on a burn for a few seconds and covering it with butter.
items.pourquoi_faux: A few seconds of cooling is not enough, and fat holds heat in the skin and brings germs.
items.correction_markdown: Cool it under cool running water for at least ten minutes, then cover loosely with a clean dressing.

items.erreur_markdown: Taking the pulse with the thumb.
items.pourquoi_faux: The thumb has its own pulse, so you may count your own beat instead.
items.correction_markdown: Use the fingertips of two fingers on the wrist.

items.erreur_markdown: Removing a blood-soaked pad from a wound to look at it.
items.pourquoi_faux: This tears the clot that is starting to form and the bleeding starts again.
items.correction_markdown: Leave the pad in place and add another on top, then keep pressing.

items.erreur_markdown: Writing that first aid means treatment given in hospital by a doctor.
items.pourquoi_faux: First aid is the immediate help given before a doctor or nurse arrives.
items.correction_markdown: Define it as immediate help given to an injured or suddenly ill person before medical help arrives.

items.enonce_markdown: (a) Give the aims of first aid by completing the sentences: to save ____, to prevent the condition from getting ____, and to help ____. (b) State where on the body a home nurse takes the pulse. (c) Name two items found in a first aid kit that are used for covering a wound.
items.solution_markdown: (a) **Life; worse; recovery**. (b) **The wrist**, using the fingertips. (c) Any two of **sterile gauze dressing, adhesive plaster, bandage**.

items.enonce_markdown: A nurse counts 19 beats of a patient's pulse in 15 seconds. A second patient has 39 beats in 30 seconds. (a) Find the pulse rate of each patient in beats per minute. (b) Which of these two patients are within the usual resting range of 60 to 80 beats a minute? (c) A third patient has 25 beats in 15 seconds just after running. Find the pulse rate and give a reason for the result.
items.solution_markdown: (a) First patient: $19 \times 4 = 76$, so **76 beats per minute**. Second patient: $39 \times 2 = 78$, so **78 beats per minute**. (b) Both are between 60 and 80, so **both** are within the usual resting range. (c) $25 \times 4 = 100$, so **100 beats per minute**. It is higher because exercise makes the heart beat faster to supply the muscles with more oxygen.

items.enonce_markdown: A family prepares a first aid box with these items (assumed prices): 3 bandages at $400$ FCFA each, 10 sterile gauze pads at $100$ FCFA each, 20 adhesive plasters at $25$ FCFA each, 1 bottle of antiseptic at $1\,500$ FCFA, 1 pair of scissors at $1\,000$ FCFA and 2 pairs of gloves at $600$ FCFA each. (a) Find the total cost. (b) The family has $8\,000$ FCFA. How much is left? (c) State one more item that the family could buy and say what it is used for. (d) State two rules for keeping the box.
items.solution_markdown: (a) Bandages: $3 \times 400 = 1\,200$. Gauze: $10 \times 100 = 1\,000$. Plasters: $20 \times 25 = 500$. Antiseptic: $1\,500$. Scissors: $1\,000$. Gloves: $2 \times 600 = 1\,200$. Total: $1\,200 + 1\,000 + 500 + 1\,500 + 1\,000 + 1\,200 = 6\,400$, so **$6\,400$ FCFA**. (b) $8\,000 - 6\,400 = 1\,600$, so **$1\,600$ FCFA** is left. (c) Any one of: tweezers, to remove splinters; adhesive tape, to hold dressings; a thermometer, to check body temperature; safety pins, to fasten bandages; cotton wool, to clean around a wound. (d) Any two of: keep it dry and labelled; keep it out of the reach of small children; check it regularly and replace used or old items; keep it where everyone can find it.

items_markdown: First aid is the immediate help given to an injured or suddenly ill person before medical help arrives; its aims are to save life, prevent worsening and help recovery.
Bleeding: press firmly with a clean pad and raise the part. Burns and scalds: cool under cool running water for at least ten minutes and cover loosely; never use butter or oil.
The pulse is taken at the wrist with the fingertips, not the thumb; about 60 to 80 beats a minute at rest in a healthy adult.
A first aid kit holds plasters, gauze dressings, bandages, cotton wool, antiseptic, scissors, tape, gloves, safety pins, tweezers and a thermometer.
Stay calm, deal with the most serious problem first, and send for medical help when necessary.
For "outline seven items" write seven different items.
